sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Golden Order Greatsword** is a Greatsword, a melee armament in Elden Ring. It is one of the Legendary Armaments.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Received upon defeating the Misbegotten Crusader in Cave of the Forlorn, located in the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
While a pure Faith build would be expected to be strongest investment in terms of pure Attack Rating (AR) for this weapon, after Faith reaches 50 Dexterity will grant roughly equal AR until it also reaches 50. The first option will grant stronger casting, more damage from the skill and potentially also higher melee damage if an enemy has lower or equal Holy defence to its Physical defence. The second option grants slightly quicker casting and potentially slightly better damage if an enemy has higher Holy defence than Physical defence.

This is one of the few weapons that deal 20% bonus damage to Undead enemies such as Skeletons and Death Rite Birds and will also prevent the former from resurrecting without needing an extra hit to finish them off.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Guardian Golems** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Golems are giant stone warriors said to have been made with an impure crystal by a golem crafter long ago. They were built to defend a civilization now gone to ruin. Though many are long broken, some golems still protect the ancient ruins.

Their hard, stone bodies are very resistant to physical damage, and Fire and lava can be seen through the plates on their chests. They can eject streams of fire through their helmet. Many golems carry massive Golem's Halberds with surprising reach that can tear the earth asunder. Others fire Golem Greatbows with great precision.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Halberd)
sections.markdown: A golem carrying massive Golem's Halberd with surprising reach that can tear the earth asunder. It can eject streams of fire through its helmet.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Greatbow)
sections.markdown:
A golem carrying a massive greatbow. It pulls back the hardy string with its immense strength to shoot great arrows infused with the storm.

Almost defenseless at melee range since they can't point their bow further down at that point. The actual danger lies mostly in approaching them, after that the stomps should be of minimal difficulty.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Magic Greatbow)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:

- Immune to all Status Effects.
- They topple and collapse to the ground when their Stance is broken, exposing a Critical Attack spot on their chests.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Golden Lightning Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Guaranteed Drop:** Crumbling Farum Azula
- Drops from a Scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, near an Ancient Dragon.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Lightning damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Overall a very strong defensive incantation, and one that comes just before the final Lightning-heavy area in the game, Crumbling Farum Azula, and the Dragonlord, one of the more Lightning-focused bosses in the game.
- Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Lightning damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60).
 - As an example, if Lightning damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Lightning damage negation.
 - Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Lightning damage negation.
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Lightning damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Golden Vow** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Grants an Aura Buff to the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius that increases all damage dealt by 15% (7.5% in PvP) and decreases all damage taken by 10% (5% in PvP) for 80 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast.
- Can be held indefinitely if the caster wants to wait for their allies to step into range of the buff.
- Generally considered the strongest of all Aura Buffs due to having the second strongest universal attack and defense bonuses (highest against other players) after the unique skill Rallying Standard while also having the longest.
 - The only real disadvantage is that the cost is relatively high (though low for the very good duration) and the moderate Faith requirement.
 - The Rallying Standard skill does have the advantage of higher bonuses (though not in PvP), while the Shared Order skill at the cost of having no defense bonus, a lower attack bonus, and a slightly shorter duration of 60 seconds has no requirement beyond being able to wield an infusible weapon such as the Dagger and a lower FP cost of 20.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- While most things in-game only gained different values against other players after Patch 1.07, this incantation seems to have gained its PvP values with or prior to Patch 1.03.
- Patch 1.09.1 fixed a bug where the effects of some Skills, Incantations, Items, and Weapons that increased attack power were not applied to Spells and Incantations.
 - After this patch, the effect of Golden Vow applied to Spells again.
- Patch 1.09 fixed a bug that reduced the power of some skills while under the Golden Vow effect.
 - This update also introduced a bug where Golden Vow's effect was not applied to Spells.
 - The bug that was fixed appears to be the same one as the one that was fixed with Patch 1.05, below, which was apparently reintroduced with Patch 1.07.
- Patch 1.05 fixed a bug that caused the attack power of some skills to be reduced when using the "Golden Vow" skill.
 - The bug would cause some skills, such as Storm Blade, to deal no damage, while others, like Waterfowl Dance, would deal heavily reduced damage.
 - This bug appears to have been introduced with one of the 4 updates from Patch 1.03 to Patch 1.03.3.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Decreases Stamina damage taken from attacks when Guarding by 20%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Since the decrease to Stamina damage when guarding is a percentage of the Stamina damage otherwise taken it sees diminishing returns when paired with equipment with high Guard Boost, such as Greatshields.
 - This means it overall pairs better with equipment that has Guard Boost in the 40 to 60 range, such as Greatswords, Colossal Weapons, and Medium Shields.
 - Effectively increases Guard Boost by an amount equal to 100 subtracted by the equipment's actual boost and then divided by 5 (i.e. (100-(Guard Boost))/5).
 - For a piece of equipment with 40 Guard Boost wearing this talisman would effectively give it 40 + (100-40)/5 = 40 + 12 = 52 Guard Boost. For comparison, something with 60 Guard Boost would effectively get 60 + (100-60)/5 = 68 Guard Boost and something with 80 Guard Boost would effectively get 80 + (100-80)/5 = 84 Guard Boost.
- Before Patch 1.04 this talisman could bring the then-not-yet-nerfed Fingerprint Stone Shield to 100 Guard Boost, decreasing Stamina damage taken to 0 and making it near impossible to deal with unless using anti-block weapons such as Reapers or the Shotel, skills such as Piercing Fang and Impaling Thrust, or by managing to circle around the shield-wielder for a Backstab.

 - While all other pieces of equipment received a 10% increase to Guard Boost this update made it so that Greatshields received a lesser increase to Guard Boost.

sections.markdown: Goldmask** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Goldmask is a Tarnished scholar and staunch Golden Order fundamentalist. He predicted the guidance of Grace, and upon being beckoned by it he came to the Lands Between to contemplate the Golden Order.

Although a Golden Order fundamentalist himself, Goldmask was critical of the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, lamenting that their learnedness had been reduced to fanatical raving and an obsession with finding a great evil to contend with, a concept which he did not believe existed within the Golden Order.

While contemplating the Erdtree in the Altus Plateau Goldmask is approached by Brother Corhyn, a man of the cloth who wished to travel alongside him as a scholar. In Leyndell, Goldmask becomes perplexed by the identity of Radagon, whose existence calls into question the principle that Queen Marika the Eternal is the one true god. With the help of the The Tarnished, Goldmask learns that Radagon is Marika.

Goldmask and Corhyn then travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, where Corhyn becomes aware of Goldmask's suspicions regarding the holism of the Golden Order. Corhyn begins to doubt Goldmask's faith, questioning his decision to travel to the Mountaintops.

Goldmask had come to the revelation that the imperfection of the Golden Order and the instability of ideology was due to the fickleness of the gods. After the Erdtree burns, Goldmask returns to Leyndell and dies on the hill near the Erdtree Sanctuary, leaving behind the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which would allow the Golden Order to be perfected.

sections.heading: Basic Info
sections.markdown: Goldmask cannot be made hostile, and will disappear if attacked, giving no Runes or item drops. He will reappear in his last location after resting at a Site of Grace.

1. Mountaintops of the Giants

 - After reloading the area, return to Goldmask's corpse to retrieve Goldmask's Rags, Gold Bracelets, and Gold Waistwrap.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Godefroy the Grafted** is an optional mini-boss in Elden Ring found in the Altus Plateau at the Golden Lineage Evergaol.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.markdown:
A member of the Golden Lineage, he is a descendant of Godfrey, First Elden Lord, and Queen Marika the Eternal. Much like his kinsman Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy has practised the grotesque act of grafting.

At some point while the alliance of the Shardbearers still ruled over Leyndell, Royal Capital, Godefroy plotted to seize control of the capital. The demigod apparently managed to recruit an army that assumed strong enough for the attack. Godefroy also made use of the special characteristic of his Shaman flesh, grafting into his body parts of corpses in an attempt to gain more strength.

Godefroy would lead his men into what would become known as the First Defense of Leyndell, but ended up fighting around the Second Church of Marika, in the middle of Altus and well distant from even the outer walls of the capital.. The demigod and his soldiers would suffer a complete defeat at the hands of soldiers of Leyndell with their leader captured by Knight Kristoff, a member of the Ancient Dragon Cult of the capital.

Godefroy was imprisoned in the Golden Lineage Evergaol with only his axe in a secluded area close to the Grand Lift of Dectus and guarded by Vulgar Militia men. Though he was defeated, the demigod's attack would precipitate the deterioration of the sovereign alliance between the Shardbearers caused by the traces of the Night of Black Knives still lingering. This would eventually lead to the demigods clashing against each other and the following wars of the Shattering.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Godefroy possessed the Godfrey Icon, a legendary talisman depicting Godfrey and Serosh, the patriarch and guide the Golden Lineage even during his imprisonment.
- Godefroy had access to the corpses of Trolls and Banished Knights with the power of the storm to graft to his body.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
Players who encounter Godefroy have most likely already defeated his relative, Godrick the Grafted. The same strategies used to defeat Godrick can be used here, since Godefroy uses the same moveset as Godrick's first phase, but without the second phase.

Be aware that he is considerably tankier, having twice as much HP as Godrick (12.5k vs 6k) and not being able to summon anything or anyone in his arena. He will also deal much more damage, even for his location.

Upon defeating Godefroy, he drops the Godfrey Icon.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Gloam-Eyed Queen** is a unseen character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by the Two Fingers long ago. She had a special eye and an affinity for god-slaying Rune of Death, manipulating its black flames in her palm and into her Godslayer's Greatsword. She embraced the highborn Godskin Nobles, needle-bearing servants of Destined Death, and cradled newborn Godskin Apostles in a swaddling cloth sewn from supple skin. Like their predecessors, the apostles assimilated serpentine physiology in a manner akin to the Crucible, and grew to bring death to the gods. Several Fire Monks abandoned their posts to swear fealty as Blackflame Monks.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen led the Godskin Apostles during a victorious god-hunt, however, she was defeated by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast of Queen Marika. Afterward, Marika removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it away within his Black Blade, creating the Golden Order and suppressing the true power of the Godslayer incantations. The Gloam-Eyed Queen's sword was locked away at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid and her Godskin Swaddling Cloth is in Spiritcaller's Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants, guarded by a Spiritcaller Snail that summons the spirits of Godskin Apostles.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Golden Order** (黄金律, *Ōgonritsu*) is a philosophical and theological movement in Elden Ring. It refers to the removal of the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and the historic reign of Queen Marika the Eternal. Its greatest symbols are the Erdtree and the Grace of Gold. It is the dominant set of beliefs in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Prior to the Golden Order, the Rune of Death was part of the Elden Ring. Its power was wielded as the god-slaying black flame by the Empyrean known as the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who led the Godskin Apostles on their god hunt. The apostles' purge ended in defeat when Maliketh, Marika's half-brother and Shadowbound Beast, triumphed over the Gloam-Eyed Queen. Destined Death was subsequently removed from the Elden Ring and sealed away by Maliketh inside his Black Blade, and he became known as the "Death of the Demigods."

sections.heading: Golden Order
sections.markdown:
The confinement of the Rune of Death marked the beginning of the Golden Order. With its establishment, Marika suppressed the power of her rival and granted immortality to herself and her demigod offspring, the Golden Lineage.

The Golden Order was a governing principle, a religion, and a philosophy. It was founded on the principle that Marika was the one true god, and was propagated by the Two Fingers. It replaced the concept of Destined Death with that of Erdtree Burial.

The Golden Order was capable of integrating conflicting ideologies and practices. The dragon cult of the royal capital was compatible because the ancient dragons' lightning was imbued with gold. Later, the Erdtree faith absorbed the practice of glintstone sorcery. Concepts that threatened to shatter the Order entirely, such as life in death, were labeled as heresy and violently persecuted by the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Golden Order Fundamentalism
sections.markdown:
Golden Order Fundamentalism was a scholarly pursuit that combined both intelligence and faith. It attempted to interpret the fundamentals of the Golden Order. Fundamentalism was based on two concepts: the Law of Regression, the pull of meaning and the yearning to converge; and the Law of Causality, the pull between meanings which links all things in a chain of relation.

Among the Golden Order Fundamentalists were the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, who abandoned learning in search of an absolute evil to contend with. Miquella, who once created Fundamentalist incantations to give to his father Radagon, abandoned Fundamentalism as it could not treat Malenia's rot. Other notable followers of Golden Order Fundamentalism included Brother Corhyn, Goldmask, and the twins D. Hunter of the Dead and D, Beholder of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - The Japanese term *ōgonritsu* (黄金律, lit. "golden law") refers to the Golden Rule, the maxim of reciprocity whereby one should treat others as one would want to be treated by them ("Do unto others as you would have them do unto you").

sections.markdown: Golden Epitaph** is a straight sword and melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Found at the entrance of Auriza Hero's Grave. Requires a Stonesword Key to access and is guarded by a Basilisk.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The skill, Last Rites, functions as an Aura Buff and adds 25 Holy damage and a universal 10% (5% for PvP) damage bonus, as well as a 100% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death. While being an Aura Buff does mean it will stack with a lot of other buffs, it also places it in competition with Golden Vow (especially the spell version), which also adds a strong boost to damage negation on top of its damage boost, and the Golden Epitaph being Faith-leaning means meetings its requirements are easy.
 - However, Last Rites is generally quicker to use and doesn't require a Sacred Seal to use, making it possibly more convenient in combat.
- This weapon has an innate 30% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death (Skeletons, Deathbirds and such), on top of dealing the Holy damage that they are usually vulnerable to.
- Has the most Attack Power (AP) on a hybrid Strength/Faith build or a hybrid Dexterity/Faith build, with a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build being a bit weaker, and a pure Faith build being weaker still.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:

- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- An epitaph is "a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone" (Cambridge Dictionary), which in this case would be the phrase "O brother, lord brother, please die a true death." in the description.
- This weapons resembles the Rune Sword from Demon's Souls.
- Patch 1.12 fixed a bug that caused damage to the player and friendly summons when using the "Last Rites" Skill under specific circumstances.
 - Prior to the fix, Last Rites would be applied to non-damaging, persistent effects such as Terra Magica, making them deal the flat 25 Holy damage to any friendly players standing on it.
- Patch 1.07 increased effect duration, increased attack power, effect against Those Who Live in Death has been revised upward.
 - The skill's duration was increased from 45 seconds to 60 seconds, the universal 10% damage buff was added (limited to 5% in PvP), and the damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death was increased from 50% to 100%.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed.
 - For the skill, that is.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Gurranq, Beast Clergyman**, also known as **Beast Clergyman** and **Maliketh, the Black Blade**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Gurranq is a hulking, bestial high clergyman from Farum Azula who resides in the Bestial Sanctum in north-eastern Caelid. Long ago, his terrifying ferocity earned him the name "Death of the Demigods. Presently, he seeks Deathroot, a product of the Rune of Death which spread through the Lands Between following the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Gurranq consumes Deathroot, although it does not appear to sate him.

Gurranq was assisted in his eradication of the Deathroot by D, Hunter of the Dead, a hunter of Those Who Live in Death. However, D passes this duty onto a Tarnished after noticing their prowess for weeding Deathroot. The Tarnished brings the Deathroot they find throughout the world to Gurranq, and is given access to bestial incantations in exchange. Once they have fed Gurranq all the Deathroot they can find, Gurranq leaves the sanctum. Although still not sated, he realises that he can do no more, and that his appetite will be his sole companion.

When the Tarnished travels to Crumbling Farum Azula to claim the Rune of Death, they encounter Gurranq once more. If the Tarnished had given Gurranq all the Deathroots, he is saddened by his friend's betrayal, but nonetheless attacks the Tarnished to protect the Rune of Death from them. Gurranq is overwhelmed, forcing him to use the Rune of Death to empower himself and reveal his true form as Maliketh, the Black Blade, shadowbound beast of Queen Marika the Eternal. The Tarnished defeats Maliketh, and unleashes the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. *(Optional)* Speak to D, Hunter of the Dead, after obtaining a Deathroot and he will advise you to visit Gurranq. This can either be done at the start of D's questline in Limgrave, or in Roundtable Hold.
1. Travel to the Bestial Sanctum at the north-eastern point of Caelid. The sending gate marked on your map by D if you showed him a Deathroot will lead you straight there. Speak to Gurranq. If you have at least one Deathroot, Gurranq will give you a Clawmark Seal and Beast Eye. The Beast Eye will notify you whenever you are close to another Deathroot.
1. Hand over each Deathroot you find to Gurranq in exchange for rewards. After you have given him four Deathroot, reload the area and Gurranq will attack you. After depleting 30% of Gurranq's health, he will be subdued- speak to him and reload the area so that he returns to his original position.
1. After giving him the ninth Deathroot, he will give you an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone before disappearing.
1. Gurranq will reappear at the end of Crumbling Farum Azula, under the name Beast Clergyman. After reducing his health to 50% he will enter phase 2, under the name Maliketh, the Black Blade.
 - Maliketh can be fought before completing Gurranq's questline. Doing so will not affect the questline, and Gurranq will remain in the Bestail Sanctum even after Maliketh has been defeated. Likewise, killing Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum will not affect the fight against Maliketh.
 - Maliketh will have unique dialogue if you complete Gurranq's questline before fighting him in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The weapon Gurranq uses is a Cinquedea.
- Gurranq can occasionally be found outside the Bestial Sanctum at night, howling in the direction of the Erdtree.

sections.markdown: The **Haligtree** (聖樹, *Seiju*) is a great tree in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Haligtree is a massive, withering tree covered in fungi, extending from a stump in the northern Lands Between. It lies far north of Leyndell, Royal Capital, and off the coast of the Consecrated Snowfield. Pilgrims must present a secret medallion at the Grand Lift of Rold to access the Consecrated Snowfield. From there, they follow a trail of lights, cross the river to Ordina, Liturgical Town, and use a Sending Gate to reach the Haligtree.

The Haligtree is divided into two areas: Miquella's Haligtree and Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. The upper area, Miquella's Haligtree, is a sparse canopy populated by Giant Ants and Oracle Envoys. This section contains Haligtree Town, an open and organic treehouse refuge for the unwanted that features statues of the twin Demigods. The lower section, Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, is a robust stone fortress occupied by Haligtree Knights and Cleanrot Knights who serve Miquella and Malenia. Both areas are made from different materials and for different purposes, though Haligtree Town appears far newer and cleaner than the brace. Its design features more complex curved surfaces, and it has more of the intricate knotwork patterns associated with Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the Empyrean Miquella abandoned Golden Order Fundamentalism upon realizing it could not cure his twin sister Malenia's scarlet rot. Seeking to create a new order of Unalloyed Gold, he settled on the Haligtree as his sanctuary.

After the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella watered the sapling with his own Empyrean blood. He later embedded himself within a cocoon in the tree's roots to nurture it, attempting to grow it into an Erdtree. However, his efforts were interrupted when Mohg, the Lord of Blood, abducted him from the Haligtree. Under Miquella's charm, Mohg zealously sought to elevate the Empyrean to godhood and establish the Mohgwyn Dynasty as Miquella's consort. Without Miquella, the Haligtree began to wither.

Afterward, Cleanrot Knight Finlay carried Malenia's slumbering body to the Haligtree, placing her at its roots. There, Malenia awaited her brother's return while slowly corrupting the tree with the scarlet rot.

Nevertheless, the Haligtree became a refuge for societal outcasts, including the Misbegotten and Kindred of Rot. Loretta, a former Knight of Caria, established a sanctuary for the Albinaurics within its boughs, turning the area into a sacred haven for their kind.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The form of a young person with a hole in their torso can still be seen in the roots of the Haligtree where Miquella's cocoon once rested within it.
- The current Haligtree appears to have grown from the stump of the older tree originating from Miquella's cocoon.
- Haligtree game area has two sets of roots that often appear alongside one another. The larger, wider, and darker ones are older than Miquella's.

- The master of Castle Sol holding half of the Medallion required to access the Haligtree would have been allowed to enter it depending on the success of the Eclipse in reviving a soulless Demigod.
- Gideon Ofnir sought the path to the Haligtree, sending his shadow, Ensha, to retrieve the secret medallion from the Village of the Albinaurics. In the process, Ensha killed Lattena's wolf companion, Lobo, but ultimately failed in his mission.
- The Haligtree Secret Medallion depicts it with green or viridian amber.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Haligtree is a combination of the Old English word *hālig* (holy, sacred; healthy, sound) and *tree*. A literal translation would be "holy tree".
- In cut dialogue lines, Old Albus referenced a chalk city of Miquella called *"Eburion"*. This area may have been reworked into Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Grace** (祝福, *Shukufuku*), also referred to as the **Grace of Gold** (黄金の祝福, *Ōgon no Shukufuku*), is a blessing given to people throughout the Lands Between by the Elden Ring and the Erdtree that symbolizes its presence. This blessing is represented by a golden light in the eyes of the inhabitants of the Lands Between. Those who had grace bestowed on them, but later lost it, are known as Tarnished.

sections.heading: Grace
sections.markdown:
The Lands Between are blessed by the presence of the Elden Ring and by the Erdtree, which symbolizes its presence, and this has given grace or blessing to the people throughout the land, great and small.

At some point, Queen Marika the Eternal took away Grace from Godfrey, First Elden Lord and his kinfolk, turning them into Tarnished. They then left the Lands Between in an event called the Long March of the Tarnished. Long afterwards, Grace would be returned to them, or their descendants, and they would be called back to the Lands Between.

At the time of the game, when given back, Grace itself is what gives the Tarnished their life.

sections.heading: The Guidance of Grace
sections.markdown:
Sometimes, the Tarnished can see golden rays of Grace that point in a particular direction, called the Guidance of Grace. It exists to guide the Tarnished and lead them along the proper path. It was also said that the guidance of grace would ensure that a Finger Maiden be brought to her chosen Tarnished. Or at least, such was the promise long ago.

Even now, some sites of grace retain that power, and their golden rays can guide the Tarnished along the way.

It is said that true guidance awaits those with iron wills and unwavering faith, although it can be lost. In fact, most Tarnished don't even see it nowadays.

Those in distant lands who saw the guidance of grace were usually seen as undesirables, and were usually expatriated, after which they set to journey to the Lands Between. Similarly, the churches outside the Lands Between, dedicated to the teachings of the Two Fingers, sent confessors out to follow the guidance of grace.

sections.markdown:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Guardians**, also known as **Tree Guardians**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The masked guardians entered an ancient death pact with the Erdtree to be renewed with eternal life. Armed with swordspears whittled from the hard wood of old trees, they were dextrous, expert protectors of Minor Erdtrees and the Erdtree itself at Leyndell, Royal Capital. Budding branches grew from their backs, ready to release perfume and poisonous pollen. The blooming of their blood-red flowers was said to signal the impending end of their tenure, and the beginning of their transformation into trees.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.markdown: There are three variants: **Guardians**, **Putrid Guardians**, **Full Bloom Guardians**.

sections.heading: Guardian
sections.markdown: Masked guardians commonly found around Minor Erdtrees. They fight using swordspears, and have a charging attack which releases a cloud of poison.

sections.heading: Guardian (Full Bloom)
sections.markdown: Guardians with blood-red flowers blooming on their backs, said to mark the senescence of their ancient pact. They can grow additional flowers on their backs to restore their health, and can reinforce their weapons with large roots, granting them much heavier attacks.

sections.heading: Putrid Tree Guardian
sections.markdown: Guardians found in areas contaminated with Scarlet Rot, with withered roots on their backs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Internal name: **BugsEater**
- The Guardians' blades are embellished with a spiral motif.
- The gold medallion around their neck depicts a smiling, eight-pointed sun with swirling flames.

sections.markdown: Guardian Golem** is an optional boss in Elden Ring. It is located in Highroad Cave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A Guardian Golem found at the end of Highroad Cave, having most likely fallen down from the bridge to the Divine Tower of Limgrave.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
Damage types: mainly Standard damage, with some Pierce damage from its thrusts and Fire damage from its flame breaths.

It's immune to all Status Effects and has 40% negation to all non-Physical damage types except for Magic, where it has only 20% resistance. It is somewhat weak to Strike damage, having 0% negation towards it, and a mild 10% negation against all other Physical damage types.

Since it starts out lying on the ground and will take a few seconds to get up once alerted, it's easy to get in some opening hits on its ankles. It has the range advantage and can hit most of the cave thanks to the length of its weapon.

The simplest strategy is to do the same as with a regular, non-boss halberd golem by sticking behind its ankles and backing away when its starts hitting the ground with the butt of its weapon or if it breathes fire.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Graven Masses**, also known as **Graven Schools** or **Schools of Graven Mages**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The primeval sorcerers who founded the Academy of Raya Lucaria adhered to the teachings of the primeval current, collecting lesser scholars and fusing them into spherical accretions known as the seeds of stars. The Graven Masses were large orbs of glintstone crowns created through forbidden glintstone sorcery—a practice that came to haunt the academy.

Upon gaining control of the academy, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon banned all inquiry into the primeval current. The primeval sorcerers Lusat and Azur were subsequently exiled. Later, the academy’s prodigy, Sorceress Sellen, revived the practice, transforming her peers into Graven Schools. Her actions earned her the title of "Graven Witch" and led to her expulsion and imprisonment.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Graven Masses take the form of large spheres composed of human faces wearing Olivinus Glintstone Crowns and Lazuli Glintstone Crowns. These Schools of Graven Mages are strange constructs animated by sorcery. In combat, they either release a purple mist that deals magic damage, or fire magic projectiles high into the air, which then rain down on their foes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Graven Masses do not drop items.
- Sorceress Sellen's sobriquet, the "Graven Witch", implies that she may have been one of the sorcerers responsible for the creation of Graven Masses.
 - Sellen becomes a Graven Mass herself at the end of her questline, provided the player sides with her against Castellan Jerren and reports the locations of Primeval Sorcerer Azur and Primeval Sorcerer Lusat.
 - Sellen's Graven Mass includes her Witch's Glintstone Crown.
- An inanimate Graven Mass can be found in a small room adjoining the Church of the Cuckoo in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, surrounded by crystals. Floating particles resembling a starry sky can be seen around it. Azur's Glintstone Staff can be picked up just in front of it.
 - Another can be found in Albinauric Rise in the Consecrated Snowfield, from which the Graven-Mass Talisman can be obtained.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Guard Boost** is a stat in Elden Ring.

It decreases the damage to Stamina received when guarding by an equivalent percentage, i.e. a +0 Dagger with its 15 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.15)=85 Stamina damage when guarding while a +0 Brass Shield with its 61 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.61)=39 Stamina damage when guarding. For 200 base Stamina damage the equivalent numbers would be 200*(1-0.15)=170 Stamina damage for the Dagger and 200*(1-0.61)=78 Stamina damage for the Brass Shield.

sections.markdown: The **Guilty**, also known as **thorn sorcerers**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
These maidens were accused of a grave misdeed at the dawn of the Erdtree era, and the Briars of Sin crushed their eyes. Clad in the red garb of exiled criminals, the Guilty abandoned prayer when blind faith brought only despair. They dwelled in darkness until they discovered the blood star, embracing heretical thorn sorcery. They fashioned smoldering saplings into staves and transmuted sacrificial blood into red glintstone, a practice reviled by sorcerers at the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

The Guilty congregated with the Fire Monks, keepers of the Giants' Flame, and came to venerate a maiden who was reborn in the Lands Between after the Briars of Sin destroyed her eyes.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
A pale figure wearing a deep crimsom hood and bloodstained robes clutches a burning branch. Sharp briars coil around her gaunt frame, and a golden crown of thorns rests atop her head, twisting into a long trailing braid. Her nose and lips are cut off, and she screeches in agony.

These blind hexers wield faith-based sorceries that deal Fire damage and inflict Blood Loss buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Elden Ring Nightreign adds Blackflame Sorcerers, which are retextured Guilty Sorcerers that use Godslayer Incantations.
- The Guilty drop Smoldering Butterflies, which are associated with Melina.
- Blindness was a prerequisite for the Guilty to perceive the Blood Star.
- Queen Marika and Dominula Dancers also have long, single braids.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The internal names for Guilty are **DestructionsIntoFire** and **DestructionsIntoFire_Weak** (ID: 4381).
- The record for Blackflame Guilty in Elden Ring Nightreign (ID: 4386) was dummied out in the *Elden Ring* code.
- This enemy uses the same base model and animations as the Rot Disciple (ID: 4385), which wears a tall hat and uses Poison.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1]** is a Bell Bearing in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Reward**: Wyndham Catacombs
- The Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1] is obtained upon defeating the Lightning-attuned Erdtree Burial Watchdog boss at the end of the Wyndham Catacombs on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Use
sections.markdown:
Give the Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1] to the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold to expand their shop inventory. It adds the following items:
- [[item:grave-glovewort-1|Grave Glovewort [1]]] (800 Runes)
- [[item:grave-glovewort-2|Grave Glovewort [2]]] (1,200 Runes)
- [[item:grave-glovewort-3|Grave Glovewort [3]]] (1,600 Runes)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Benefits of the Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1] carry over into New Game Plus (NG+).
- The difference in cost between each rank of Grave Glovewort unlocked by this Bell Bearing is 400 Runes.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- [[item:glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-2|Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [2]]], for rank 4, 5, and 6 Grave Gloveworts.
- [[item:glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-3|Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [3]]], for rank 7, 8, and 9 Grave Gloveworts.
- [[item:ghost-glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-1|Ghost-Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1]]], for the equivalent Ghost Gloveworts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [3]** is a Bell Bearing in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot**: Crumbling Farum Azula
- The Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [3] can be found near a lake at Crumbling Farum Azula. From the Tempest-Facing Balcony site of grace, head southwest back through the church and take the elevator on the far side. Upon exiting the elevator, turn left and follow the wall until you reach an area overlooking the lake below. The item is located under a gazebo next to the lake.

sections.heading: Use

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:

- This is the only Grave Glovewort Bell Bearing where the cost increase between the three Grave Glovewort ranks is inconsistent: a 1,000 Rune increase for the first two ranks and then a 2,000 Rune increase for the third.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Golden Order Totality** is a Gesture in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Animation
sections.markdown: Locks the player character in place during the animation.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Quest Item:** Leyndell, Royal Capital
- Received from Goldmask after telling him the truth about Radagon of the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This gesture becomes unavailable for the rest of the play-through after lighting the Forge of the Giants.
- While this gesture requires 37 Intelligence in order to cast Law of Regression to solve the puzzle, it is possible for every single starting class to clear it without any Intelligence investment, through the use of Int-boosting equipment and buffs.
